To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ALC can be diagrammatically represented by Peircean existential graphs, a calculus for this diagrammatic representation can be developed, and the calculus is sound and complete.

(1) Peirce's system of existential graphs is the best suited for representing description logics diagrammatically, (2) ALC can be represented diagrammatically by means of labeled, tree-like graphs, (3) these graphs can be manipulated by a diagrammatic calculus that is equivalent to the symbolic calculus for ALC, and (4) this calculus is sound and complete.

developing a diagrammatic reasoning language that is equivalent to a well-known logic, the description logic ALC.
the development of a diagrammatic calculus for the representation of DLs.
the question of whether the diagrammatic reasoning systems can be used for reasoning with DLs, which are a well-established symbolic logic for the representation and processing of knowledge.
